summary: Retested the Prep Agent fix through the public URL. Static lint/code review confirms the undefined fetchBatches reference is gone and API URLs use REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Authenticated GET /api/prep-agent/batches returns 200 and POST returns a valid pending batch, but the POST-triggered LLM task still blocks follow-up list/detail/delete requests for over 30 seconds. The supplied account still redirects /prep-agent to /pricing because its trial is expired, so the real form could not be rendered or submitted in-browser.

critical.issue: After POST returned HTTP 200 with a valid pending batch, the immediate authenticated GET list timed out after 30s and cleanup DELETE also timed out. Progress polling is unavailable while generation runs.

integration_issues.flow: Open /prep-agent with the supplied teacher account
integration_issues.issue: Login succeeds, but /prep-agent redirects to /pricing because /api/subscription/status returns has_access=false and status=trial_expired. The requested form and browser creation flow remain untestable with the required credentials.

issues: Code uses the browser-native input[type=date] instead of the app's shadcn calendar/popover component, producing browser-dependent date-picker UX.

action_items: Offload the Prep Agent LLM workflow to a worker/job queue or thread/process boundary; asyncio.create_task alone does not prevent the LLM SDK call from blocking the sole API event loop.
Provide an active trial/subscription for test@school.edu, then rerun the real /prep-agent form and creation flow.
Replace the native date input with the standard shadcn calendar component for consistent date selection.
critical_code_review_comments: PrepAgent.js no longer calls undefined fetchBatches; polling and post-publish paths consistently call fetchBatchesUpdate, and the selected batch is synchronized from polling results.
PrepAgent.js now derives its API base from process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with /api appended; the current environment value produces the correct public endpoints.

routes/prep_agent.py uses asyncio.create_task(run_prep_agent_workflow(...)), but the observed request starvation proves the awaited LLM SDK path still blocks the single worker; task scheduling is not equivalent to execution isolation.

success_rate.backend: 67% (2/3 focused pytest tests passed; create returned valid data but post-create polling/cleanup timed out)
success_rate.frontend: 0% of requested page/form outcomes (route redirected to pricing; static regression review passed)

seed_data_creation: Created one uniquely named TEST_ prep batch. The initially timed-out DELETE was subsequently processed; authenticated listing confirmed no new TEST_ batch remained.
test_credentials: Read /app/memory/test_credentials.md and authenticated successfully as test@school.edu; /api/subscription/status reports trial_expired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use the public URL from frontend/.env. GET batches is responsive when idle (200 in about 0.14s). Reproduce blocking by POSTing a valid batch and immediately polling GET; iteration 99 timed out at 30s. Browser login redirects to /pricing. The prior stale completed batch batch_356eece6ee65 remains and was not modified.
rca_of_the_issue: POST /api/prep-agent/batches inserts and returns a valid pending record, then schedules run_prep_agent_workflow with asyncio.create_task. The workflow awaits emergentintegrations LLM calls that still monopolize the only reload-mode Uvicorn worker/event loop, so concurrent GET and DELETE requests wait until the LLM call yields/completes. Separately, ProtectedRoute reads has_access=false for the supplied account and intentionally redirects before PrepAgent mounts; therefore the original crash regression cannot be exercised through the UI with these credentials.
